goal.en: Resolve a bounded design into real repository ownership, contracts and implementable code scope.

graphPolicy.location: .starciwork node dependsOn/refs with direct sourceRefs and collocated assets

purpose.en: Read current target, ancestor scope, refs, dependencies, assertions and validator freshness. For an explicitly new target, absence is expected: inspect the nearest existing ancestor/workspace, then create only that selected scope. Preserve unaffected accepted content.

Read accepted requirements, decisions, constraints and acceptance IDs declared as relevant inputs in the selected .starciwork graph. Intent governs expected behavior; source is not a replacement. Do not invent a mandatory BA predecessor for a scope that does not require one; a needed missing input is a reported graph/scope gap, not a new dependency silently added here.

When source exists/is selected, resolve repository resource, actual checkout/root/HEAD and dirty state; read applicable instructions, manifests, owning code, callers and relevant tests. Greenfield/spec-only work records source not-yet-created and grounds intent in the user request; no invented repository or fact citation. Source implementation still needs an actual selected writable repository.

reads.path: selected resource contracts + actual package/deployment manifests

purpose.en: Read exact versions, deployment topology and data constraints; compatibility claims need source/documentation or experiments, not memory.
Read the JSON field contract and this operator procedure before authoring the .starciwork payload.

Only when explicitly selected in a job matrix, read the exact cell ID, operation, immutable input bindings, requested output JSON shapes and required criteria. Standalone execution needs no fabricated matrix request. A template is not authority for extra effects.

reads.path: profiles/registry.json + selected runtime execution profile + actual host tools/model

purpose.en: Select the actual host runtime codex or claude and this operator role from the V2-derived active profiles. Use current host model configuration; historical model names are not availability proof. Capabilities are the intersection of actual tools, selected profile policy, op permissions and existing task authority. Do not revive V2 dispatch chains, retired profiles or extra-agent permissions.

content.en: Write target ownership, call chain, contracts, data ownership and context-relevant controls, observations and gaps. Full starci/specification@2 records the source-grounded design and architectureReview. Patterns are optional and justified; do not require Saga/CQRS for every module. Preserve accepted Business outcomes and distinguish design proof from running behavior.
Record observed current source map and compatibility checks; selected alternative/risk review is design proof, not a passing runtime.

Only for a selected job matrix, return the exact request-bound result. Populate every declared cell output with actual canonical Work/source/runtime references or produced JSON artifacts from this job; retain real artifact bytes and hashes. Do not rename/regenerate upstream expectations. Missing required output/evidence remains blocked or failed and cannot advance. The selected request freezes output field schemas before execution.

action.en: Research exact FE/BE revisions, manifests, entrypoints, DI, API handlers, data stores, jobs, deploy topology and tests. Follow inbound callers and outbound consumers; cite repository/path/symbol/revision and distinguish observed paths from proposed paths. Trace each network hop from caller symbol through URL/config resolution, proxy/ingress wiring, receiving handler and deployment owner; record synchronous, async and in-process edges separately. Names and comments are clues, not endpoint proof. Keep observed and desired routing separate and block contradictory boundary decisions. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Map accepted business flow and AC IDs to responsible services and authoritative data writers. Draw the logical request/response and asynchronous event sequence in ordered flow rows, including trust boundaries; never assume a class is an independently deployed service. Write ordered serviceCalls with caller/callee service IDs, caller/receiver source refs, operation, endpoint binding, credentials/trust boundary, data classification, timeout/retry and evidence status. Verify response path and downstream side effects. Unobserved deployment/runtime facts remain unknown.

Choose the smallest design satisfying accepted invariants and actual constraints. Challenge one coherent proposal with a materially simpler alternative, trade-offs and a reasoned decision. Select concerns from real business risks, data value, scale, trust boundaries and operating model, not a universal technology checklist. Evaluate named patterns only when relevant; patternDecisions may be empty. An adopted Saga/CQRS/outbox must describe actual mechanisms, not labels or handler filenames. Specify applicable transaction, idempotency, ordering, timeout, concurrency and recovery behavior; never invent numeric targets or unresolved product policy.

Write codeImpacts with exact repository/path/symbol, observed/proposed identity, direct/transitive relation, change/preserve/review decision, reason, caller chain, tests and protected paths. Write serviceImpacts with deployable owner, inbound/outbound consumers, stores/events, compatibility, rollout/rollback and observability; explain unaffected boundaries. Map every selected pattern and service call back to exact source symbols, data/event schemas, deployment/config owners and protected paths. Do not route traffic to a different service merely because its repository contains a matching resolver.

Review each trust boundary: authentication, object/tenant authorization, validation, credential custody, sensitive logs, external provider/AI input, replay and resource abuse where relevant. Link threat, server-side control owner, code/service impact and positive/negative AC. Record residual risks and decision owner without claiming a security audit ran. Add a threat model per trust boundary: assets, entry points, attacker capability, exploit path, impact, prevention/detection, control owner and negative acceptance. Assess object/function/property authorization, tenant isolation, token issuer/audience/scope and forwarding, SSRF/redirect/DNS/egress, injection, webhook authenticity/replay, resource/AI cost abuse, sensitive transcripts/logs and dependency risks when applicable. Mark non-applicability with evidence; unresolved high-impact risks need a decision owner and block acceptance.

Produce implementation ceilings, protected paths, dependencies and required checks from actual repository scripts/CI. Lint, typecheck, tests/coverage, build and Sonar execute inside FE/BE implement; this op specifies them only. Bind rollout/migration/cleanup plans without executing them. Preserve business expected results unchanged. Design failure-injection tests for wrong service target, unauthorized forwarding, stale reads, duplicate/out-of-order messages, crash after commit before publish, compensation failure and retry exhaustion as applicable; implementations run them. Author canonical user journeys and journeyCoverage links to flow/AC IDs using the shared journey contract; preserve accepted journeys unchanged in architecture. Do not convert internal service hops into UI actions. Browser-free scope may use an empty array only when no UAT acceptance is assigned. Record architectureReview with context-selected concerns linked to requirements, sources, concrete trigger/impact/control/owner/acceptance scenarios, decisions, residual risks and evidence limitations. Examine persistence, connections, failure domains, capacity, security, HA, backup/restore, provider or total-infrastructure loss only to the depth their consequences require in this scope. Where durable customer state is in scope, identify authoritative versus rebuildable data, all stores/volumes/config/Secrets/keys, consistency point, independent backup custody, recovery prerequisites/order and verification. Never claim every possible edge case is covered or a recovery drill ran from design prose. Current external production practices need primary sources and an explicit applicability argument.

Validate target ownership, request/data/credential paths, contracts and applicable failure controls against accepted Business and actual sources. Separate proposed design from observations and implementation gaps. Require accepted decisions for material concerns and residual risks before passing design review. Omit unnecessary Saga/CQRS designs; validate concrete mechanisms when selected. Preserve accepted SRS requirements/flows/AC and user journeys, with explicit business leaf dependencies. Architecture done means reviewed design only, never implementation, security audit, HA or executed restore proof.

requirement.en: Run workspace validation; every cited ID/path exists or is explicitly proposed, required assertions are covered, input bindings are current, and an honest not-run/fail cannot earn done.
Every selected operation has an owner, actual/proposed repo-path scope and test instrument; every required business outcome maps to a contract. No source implementation claim.

Every selected flow resolves cited code/service impact, security controls and acceptance; proposed/unknown facts remain explicit. Validate the JSON specification and .starciwork before review completion.

condition.en: An operation/store has no determined owner or required write crosses another owner without scope.
A required version, contract or migration compatibility claim lacks evidence.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.

placeholders.repo-id: Resolved direct repository name or path
